title: The east-coast gas reservation scheme starting in July 2027 will materially lower domestic gas prices
oneLiner: Australia has decided to reserve gas for domestic buyers. The question now is whether the scheme, as designed and then softened, will do what it was announced to do.
body: In May 2026 the federal government announced that Queensland's three LNG export ventures must reserve a share of export volumes for Australian users from July 2027, with contracts signed before 22 December 2025 exempt. In September 2026 the rule was recast around forecast domestic demand rather than a flat share of exports. The government says prices will fall; it will not say by how much.
contextBackground:
Until 2015 the east-coast market was isolated. The Gladstone export terminals linked domestic prices to Asian ones just as the Bass Strait fields began to decline, and east-coast prices roughly tripled. The competition regulator has run a [standing inquiry](https://www.accc.gov.au/inquiries-and-consultations/gas-inquiry-2017-30) since 2017; governments added an export-control mechanism, a price cap and a code of conduct, but not reservation.

That changed in 2026. A [Gas Market Review](https://industry.gov.au/news/australian-governments-gas-market-review-recommends-domestic-gas-reservation-policy) recommended reservation; on [7 May 2026](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-05-07/east-coast-gas-reservation-policy-announced-to-avert-shortages/106651532) the government announced a 20 per cent reservation of export volumes from July 2027, with pre-December-2025 contracts preserved. Producers split: APLNG and Shell accepted it, Santos opposed it. In September 2026 the rule was softened to reserve about 110 per cent of forecast domestic demand. See the [Wikipedia summary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_Gas_Reservation_Scheme_Australia_2027).
contextDisagreement: Nobody now disputes that reservation is happening. The argument is whether exempting existing contracts and pegging the reserve to forecast demand leaves enough new gas in the scheme to move prices before the 2030s, and whether the Greens' alternative, an export tax, would have done more.

timeline.text: Western Australia adopts a domestic reservation policy for new LNG projects.
The first Queensland LNG export cargo leaves Gladstone, linking east-coast gas to Asian prices.
The Australian Domestic Gas Security Mechanism is created. The ACCC's standing gas inquiry begins.

timeline.label: 22 Dec 2025
timeline.text: Cut-off date: export contracts signed before this are later exempted from reservation.

timeline.label: 7 May 2026
timeline.text: The government announces a 20 per cent reservation of Queensland LNG export volumes from July 2027.

timeline.label: Sep 2026
timeline.text: The rule is softened to reserve about 110 per cent of forecast domestic demand; industry welcomes the change and warns of oversupply.

otherClaim.title: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's

claimItself.title: Western Australia requires LNG projects to reserve 15 per cent of production for the domestic market, and its gas prices have been well below the east coast's
claimItself.oneLiner: The one Australian jurisdiction with reservation has had the cheapest domestic gas.
claimItself.body: Since 2006 Western Australia has negotiated a 15 per cent domestic reservation into the approval of each LNG project. Through the east-coast price spikes of 2017 and 2022 its domestic wholesale prices stayed a fraction of eastern levels.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Western Australia's low domestic gas prices owe more to abundant, cheap offshore gas and a small market than to reservation

claimItself.title: East-coast wholesale gas prices more than doubled after LNG exports from Queensland began in 2015
claimItself.oneLiner: Domestic buyers moved from an isolated market to one priced off Asian LNG, and paid for it.
claimItself.body: Before 2015, east-coast gas typically traded at $3 to $4 a gigajoule. The competition regulator's inquiry documents offers to domestic buyers rising to between $8 and $12 within three years of exports beginning, with spikes well above that in 2022.

claimItself.title: AEMO's Integrated System Plan relies on gas-fired generation to firm renewables through the 2030s and beyond
claimItself.oneLiner: The market operator's own plan keeps gas peakers in the mix as backup, run for a small number of hours a year.
claimItself.body: In every Integrated System Plan scenario, gas-fired peaking plants remain in the system to cover long periods of low wind and solar output. Their capacity is held or grows while their total energy output falls, because they run rarely.

claimItself.title: Most of the National Electricity Market's remaining coal-fired capacity is scheduled to close by the late 2030s
claimItself.oneLiner: Owners' announced closure dates, and the market operator's planning scenarios, retire the bulk of the coal fleet within fifteen years.
claimItself.body: The Australian Energy Market Operator's Integrated System Plan models the exit of most coal generation across the eastern states during the 2030s, consistent with dates announced by plant owners. Several plants have brought their dates forward rather than back.

otherClaim.title: Because export contracts signed before 22 December 2025 are exempt, the scheme reaches too little gas to move prices for years

claimItself.title: Because export contracts signed before 22 December 2025 are exempt, the scheme reaches too little gas to move prices for years
claimItself.oneLiner: Most current east-coast production is already contracted; the reserve bites only on new supply.
claimItself.body: The announced scheme preserves foundation contracts and any signed before the December 2025 cut-off. Since the three Queensland ventures sold most of their output under long-term contracts years ago, the gas actually subject to reservation is a thin slice of new and uncontracted supply, which critics say is too small to shift the domestic price before the 2030s.

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: In September 2026 the reservation was recast to about 110 per cent of forecast domestic demand, and Santos is the only major east-coast producer not already supplying the domestic market

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Modelling cited in support of the scheme found that additional Queensland supply would lower wholesale prices in New South Wales and Victoria

otherClaim.title: Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix

claimItself.title: Mandatory reservation will deter investment in new gas supply and worsen the shortfall it is meant to fix
claimItself.oneLiner: The producers' central objection: forced local sales at any price make new fields harder to finance.
claimItself.body: Australian Energy Producers argued the draft imposed complex and opaque compliance obligations, would undermine trust with Asian buyers, and would deter investment. Santos's chief executive said forcing sales at any price could 'kill companies'; a smaller producer called the scheme 'nationalisation by stealth'. If new supply does not come, the argument runs, prices rise regardless of reservation.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Two of the three Queensland LNG ventures accepted a reservation scheme; only Santos opposed it

otherClaim.title: Higher east-coast gas prices are the market working: they signal scarcity and speed up the shift away from gas

claimItself.title: Higher east-coast gas prices are the market working: they signal scarcity and speed up the shift away from gas
claimItself.oneLiner: If gas is scarce and the grid must decarbonise anyway, a high price is doing the right job.
claimItself.body: Reservation holds domestic prices below the international price, which encourages continued gas use and discourages the electrification and efficiency that the energy transition requires. A price that reflects scarcity moves households and industry off gas faster than any policy could.

otherClaim.title: The Australian Domestic Gas Security Mechanism, in force since 2017, already lets the government limit LNG exports when a domestic shortfall is forecast

claimItself.title: The Australian Domestic Gas Security Mechanism, in force since 2017, already lets the government limit LNG exports when a domestic shortfall is forecast
claimItself.oneLiner: An export-control lever already exists; the question is whether it is the right one.
claimItself.body: The mechanism allows the minister to require exporters to find offsetting domestic supply, or restrict exports, in a year the market operator forecasts a shortfall. It has been reformed to allow quarterly rather than annual triggering, but it has never been formally activated.

otherClaim.title: CSIRO's GenCost report finds firmed renewables the cheapest new-build electricity for Australia and large-scale nuclear the most expensive

claimItself.title: CSIRO's GenCost report finds firmed renewables the cheapest new-build electricity for Australia and large-scale nuclear the most expensive
claimItself.oneLiner: The national science agency's annual cost comparison puts wind and solar with storage and transmission below every other new-build option.
claimItself.body: GenCost, produced each year by CSIRO with the market operator, estimates the cost of building and running each generation technology in Australian conditions. Its recent editions find renewables with firming cheaper per megawatt-hour than new coal, gas or nuclear, and put large-scale nuclear at the top of the range because of its capital cost and build time.

otherClaim.title: Australia should tax gas exports rather than reserve gas for domestic buyers

claimItself.title: Australia should tax gas exports rather than reserve gas for domestic buyers
claimItself.oneLiner: The competing proposal from the Greens and Senator Pocock: price the exports, do not ration them.
claimItself.body: Instead of requiring producers to set gas aside, an export levy would make overseas sales less attractive relative to domestic ones and return revenue to the public. The Greens argued the reservation policy was written by the industry for the industry; Senator David Pocock's dissenting report to a Senate committee recommended a 25 per cent tax on all gas exports. The government ruled out gas tax increases in the May 2026 budget, citing fuel security during the Middle East conflict.

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: A tax on gas exports would lower domestic gas prices

ownArguments.label: FOR
ownArguments.text: An export tax would raise public revenue that a reservation scheme forgoes
